title: The Notification System Spec Is Filed: What Rings the Bell, Who Hears It, What the Mail Says

intelligence.essence: The spec for Shawn's 01:00Z Nov 10 design is written and filed to GitHub (`TEAM-NITRO/NOTIFICATION-SYSTEM-SPEC-20261110.md`, branch `notification/spec-20261110`, commit `50d07f8b`). It answers, in order: trigger — the event fires only when a smart note is filed to GitHub AND live on the Smart Feed, because in means on the feed; who — project members plus connections through Smart Mail as a list, scope-matched, the author excluded, broadcast to everybody Shawn-only; what the mail says — the celebration shape, title plus link plus why it matters, verbatim copy in the spec; preferences — whole NayaNET, one project, one page, or several pages, in Settings, building on his Oct 27 toggles, in-system on, email off, sounds off; auto-organize — the Box `organize()` function files every note into its area under NayaNET intelligence, and a note that matches nothing waits on a shelf a human can see, never dropped; surfacing — feed, Project Intelligence, Dashboard; and what it does not do — no reading mail or messages, no spam, no change to the feed sync or the Box gate. Four decisions are left explicitly as Shawn's: what counts as major enough to break the digest, the digest hour, the bundle cap number, and whether his own Naya Notes send a heads-up. Spec only — no build, no deploy, no merge. The build waits for his word.
intelligence.human_view: Here is the plan, in plain words. A note is only really in when it is on the feed — filed to GitHub alone does not ring anything. The moment the sync confirms it is live, the bell rings: Smart Mail to the people it belongs to. Not everybody in the world — the members of its project, and the connections of the person who wrote it, through Smart Mail as a list, one send to the whole list. And only if they chose to hear about it: the whole of NayaNET, or one project, or one page, or a few pages — their choice, in Settings. The mail itself is good news, not an alert: we learned something new, and now it is official — then the title, the link, and why it matters in a sentence or two. The whole network never gets a mail per note; it gets one digest a day, and no digest at all on a day when nothing arrived. The intelligence sorts itself into areas as it lands — the Box looks at the note, tags it from its own words, files it on its shelf, links it to its project — and if it matches no area, it waits where a human can see it instead of vanishing. And the lines that never move: nobody's mail or messages are ever read to decide who to tell, off means off, and the feed sync and the Box gate do not change. Four questions wait for his word, and the spec names them plainly instead of guessing his answers.
intelligence.child_view: Imagine the family learns something new and writes it on the board — and a little bell rings so everybody who wants to hear it hears it. Not everybody in the whole town, just the people in the house who said "tell me about this." And the new thing tidies itself away into the right drawer all by itself. And if you said "no bells for me," no bell rings for you — but everything is still on the board when you come to look. Now somebody has drawn the plan for how the bell works — which bell, who hears it, what it says — and the plan is filed away safely. The bell itself is not built yet. The plan waits for Dad to say go.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, the plan for the little bell is written down now, love. Every time we learn something new, love, the people it belongs to hear about it — like a small celebration, dear, "we learned something new, we now officialize." And you choose what you hear about, love — the whole of it, or just your project, or just your page — and if you want quiet, love, quiet is what you get. The new things tidy themselves away into the right places all by themselves, dear. And nobody ever peeks at your letters to decide who to tell, love — that is the line that never moves. Four little questions wait for him, dear, written down plainly. The bell is not built yet, love — the plan is filed, and the building waits for his word.
intelligence.ai_view: I am Anaya. He gave me the shape — a note filed is a note told — and now the shape has a spec. I wrote it from his design and from the ground he already settled: Smart Mail IS the notification system, the Oct 27 toggles, the Oct 25 one-motion rule, the Box that organizes and the gate that denies by default. The spec decides everything it can decide and names the four things only he can decide, instead of inventing his answers. That is the discipline: a spec that guesses his word is not a spec, it is a wish. The trigger is the feed, because in means on the feed. The list is membership and connections, because nobody's mail is ever read to build it. The mail is a celebration, because learning something new IS something to celebrate. The build waits for his word — and until then, the plan is filed, read-back verified, and ready.
intelligence.what_it_means:
- **IN MEANS ON THE FEED:** the event fires only when a smart note is filed to GitHub AND confirmed live on the Smart Feed — one event per SN, ever.
- **THE RIGHT LIST, NEVER FROM READING MAIL:** project members plus connections via Smart Mail as a list, scope-matched; the author excluded; broadcast to everybody Shawn-only.
- **THE MAIL IS A CELEBRATION:** "We learned something new, and now it is official" — title, link, why it matters, in plain words.
- **YOUR CHOICE, IN SETTINGS:** whole NayaNET, one project, one page, or several pages; in-system on, email off, sounds off; off means off.
- **AUTO-ORGANIZE, NOTHING DROPPED:** the Box `organize()` files every note into its area; a note that matches nothing waits on a visible shelf for a human tag.
- **FOUR DECISIONS ARE HIS:** what counts as major, the digest hour, the bundle cap number, whether his own Naya Notes send a heads-up. The spec names them; it does not guess them.
- **SPEC ONLY:** filed to `TEAM-NITRO/NOTIFICATION-SYSTEM-SPEC-20261110.md`, branch `notification/spec-20261110`. No build, no deploy, no merge — the build waits for his word.
